newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks end down after inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks end down after inflation data.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares finished lower on Tuesday, hit by inflation figures and a market focus on new issues, dealers said.
The ZSE's key industrial index lost 9.64 points to close Tuesday at 10,291.03, after being depressed by losses on a number of heavyweight counters.

Dealers said stocks may trend lower in the coming week on the back of the higher February inflation data which might induce some funds to go liquid in anticipation of a rise in money market rates, brokers said on Tuesday.
The all-items consumer price index rose to 19 percent year-on-year from 15.8 percent in January largely due to increases in the prices of fuel, milk, bread and the staple maize-meal.

"The latest inflation figure may have an impact on the market. Some funds may decide to go liquid now in anticipation of rising interest rates and this may have a depressive impact on the market," one broker said.
They said a focus on a couple of planned new issues might also put pressure on some counters on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange (ZSE) for the rest of the week.
Among the day's losers, newly-listed agro-industrial company CFI shed 15 cents to 200 with brokers saying it had fallen slightly out of favour with market players after its strong debut on Monday.
Merchant bankers FMB slid 400 cents to 4,600, Barclays dropped 100 cents to 3,400, sugar producer Hippo cut 60 cents to 1,500 and building and engineering company Mash lost 10 cents to 240.
A number of counters bucked the trend, notably publishers Zimpapers which leapt 1,700 cents to 5,900 on the back of what brokers said were excellent results for the year ended December 31.
Hotel and supermarket group Meikles and horticulture company Ariston each rose 50 cents to 2,700 and 2,400 respectively while engineering firm Gulliver gained 40 cents to 340.
Minings were largely inactive with gold and nickel prices still in the doldrums. Falgold eased five cents to 70 but copper miner MCM put on five cents to 25.
The mining index edged 2.44 points up to 995.68.
